opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alyssa Rose (employee ID E026) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E026.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alyssa Rose (E026) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin is only for the owning role (Payroll Specialist). Requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for Alyssa Rose (E026) shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training; never admin). Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR records Alyssa Rose as full-time (max write for Payroll), but Security records her as a contractor with basic security training (max read for Payroll; write requires advanced training). Given the conflicting evidence, I apply the more restrictive, safe interpretation. Granting write would violate policy if the contractor record is correct, whereas read is within policy under both interpretations. Grant read (the maximum permitted under the contractor interpretation, and no more than requested).
